\paragraph{Synthesis.}
Image tokens remain instruction-blind; the readout is the sole multimodal convergence point.
Training shifts routing from mid-depth to entry-exit (L0--L1, L31), with effects at the readout ($R^2$ $+0.069$) rather than images ($\Delta \leq 1.7\%$).
This explains the visual dominance of Grant et al.~\cite{grant2026}: DINOv2 has the highest geometric alignment ($\rho = 0.692$), yet VLA readout surpasses it in decodability ($R^2 = 0.678$ vs.\ $0.634$).
Three independent analyses converge on L1 as the routing hub: attention shows training-dependent entry-exit reorganization (\S\ref{sec:learned_routing}), representational probes show an ablation gradient confined to L1 ($R^2$ $+0.059$ at L1, $+0.018$ at L8, $\approx 0$ at L13), and dose-response ablation confirms monotonic divergence ($d = 0.482 \to 0.639$; Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}). L1 ablation alters $72.3\%$ of tokens ($d = 0.65$), linking routing to output.

\paragraph{Mechanistic interpretation.}
Per-layer RSA bifurcates after L12 (Figure~\ref{fig:rsa_perlayer_curve}): readout $\rho$ declines gradually while image\_mean drops sharply ($\to 0.422$).
L1 ablation demonstrates causal influence ($z = -2.73$ vs.\ random subsets), confined to L1 ($|\Delta R^2| < 0.02$ at deeper layers).
The $R^2$ improvement reflects information gain (removing routing signals frees bandwidth); the gripper-concentrated trajectory effect ($72.3\%$ divergence) reflects discrete manipulation sensitivity.
The attention analysis reveals what the model learns (reorganized routing); ablation reveals the distributed implementation.
Per-head bootstrap CIs confirm: individual control heads produce stronger effects than instruction heads ($d = 0.051$ vs.\ $0.027$, $p = 0.002$), yet 24 instruction heads collectively generate a larger perturbation ($d = 0.65$ vs.\ $0.41$). The dose-response curve (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}) reveals a concentrated core with diminishing returns beyond 20 heads (Appendix~\ref{sec:action_trajectory}).

\paragraph{Predictions.}
Other decoder-only VLAs (e.g., RT-2) should show similar entry-layer routing reorganization given the shared causal-mask constraint; cross-attention architectures (e.g., $\pi_0$) should differ.
L1 ablation on a fine-tuned model should produce measurable task degradation on instruction-discriminative tasks.
$R^2$ measures linear decodability; action output reflects the full nonlinear forward pass. Ablation simplifies the probe's predictive subspace while altering discrete output; the two effects are complementary.

\paragraph{Limitations and scope.}
We study OpenVLA-7B on LIBERO. OpenVLA shares the dominant VLA design with RT-2~\cite{brohan2023_rt2} and $\pi_0$~\cite{black2024_pi0}; C1 follows from shared architectural constraints, but C2 may differ across backbone scales and decoder paradigms (Appendix~\ref{sec:ood_diagnostics},~\ref{sec:cka_appendix}).
Our analyses are representational and open-loop; connecting routing reorganization to task success requires closed-loop evaluation, which we leave to future work.
